[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | prefers | The author says the Sheikh’s inference is not decisive: Abu al-Baqa’s alternative coordinates جاء with كنتم and construes it as وإن جاء, a more evident parse.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | منكم is an adjective of أحد in the nominative, attached to an omitted element; من الغائط attaches to جاء as its object.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The majority form الغائط originally means low-lying ground, then euphemistically denotes the bodily event; غاط means going far out of sight, whereas تغوط means defecating.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masud reads الغيط; Ibn Jinni analyzes it as a shortened فيعل form, like هين and ميت.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · غير مسمى | reports | A second analysis treats الغيط as a verbal noun, with dialect forms غاط يغيط غيطا and غاط يغوط غوطا.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | rejects | Abu al-Baqa calls الغيط a verbal noun of يغوط and explains its yāʾ as substituted wāw; the author objects that he missed the distinct yāʾ dialect.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#5/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · حمزة والكسائي | reports | Hamza and al-Kisai read لمستم here and in 5:6; the others read لامستم. | mentions 5:6
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The فَ in فلم تجدوا coordinates what follows with the conditional clause.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The object being wiped is omitted here and stated in 5:6 with منه, so this wording is understood in light of that verse. | mentions 5:6
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa instead attaches فلم تجدوا to جاء, since on his analysis جاء coordinates with كنتم and itself forms the condition.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The فَ in فتيمموا is the response to the condition.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The command’s pronoun covers every previously named person: the sick, traveler, one coming from the toilet, and one who touched or was touched.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The shift to third person euphemistically avoids directly naming an embarrassing act; the source calls this elegant expression and compares 26:80. | mentions 26:80
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | وجد here means لقي and therefore takes one object.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | صعيدا is the direct object of تيمموا, meaning ‘intend’; the proposed analysis with an omitted preposition is not a valid analogy.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | بوجوهكم attaches to امسحوا; Abu al-Baqa regards the preposition باء as extra.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43#6/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · سيبويه | reports | Alternatively, باء is transitive: Sibawayh records مسحت رأسه وبرأسه, like نصحته ونصحت له.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · غير مسمى | reports | One interpretation supplies an omitted مضاف: ‘the places of prayer,’ meaning mosques; the exception for crossing a path supports this in one reading.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · غير مسمى | reports | A further reading سكارى with fatḥa on sīn and alif is a broken plural, by analogy with ندمان/ندامى and عطشان/عطاشى.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The root sense of السكر is closure: intoxication blocks the link between a person and reason; the term usually means loss of reason through drink, but can also describe anger, love, and similar causes.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r12] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The cited line’s repeated سكر witnesses metaphorical intoxication by love alongside literal wine intoxication.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · غير مسمى | reports | Alternatively, there is no ellipsis: the prohibition concerns approaching prayer itself in this state.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | أنتم سكارى is a subject–predicate clause functioning as a circumstantial clause of the subject of تقربوا.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | prefers | The majority read سكارى with damma on sīn and alif; the author prefers analyzing it as a broken plural, as Sibawayh does.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن الباذش | reports | Ibn al-Badhish attributes to Sibawayh the alternative analysis that سكارى is a collective noun, arguing no plural pattern has this form.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · السيرافي | reports | Al-Sirafi records the disagreement and favors analyzing سكارى as a broken plural.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأعمش | reports | Al-A'mash reads سكرى with damma on sīn and a still kāf, construing it as a feminine singular adjective on فعلى applied to a group.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari reports جناح بن حبيش’s paired forms كسلى/كسلى, with the kāf rounded and open, as comparable adjective usage.
[SAMIN-DURR:4:43/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النخعي | reports | Al-Nakha‘i reads سكرى with fatḥa on sīn and still kāf; it may be the same adjective for a group or a broken plural like جرحى, موتى, and هلكى by analogy for affliction; the discussion recalls 2:85. | mentions 2:85
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The verse forbids prayer while intoxicated enough not to know one's words and forbids a junub person from entering a mosque except to pass through without staying; this preceded the final wine prohibition.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir places the restriction in the staged prohibition of wine: after 2:219, people avoided drinking at prayer times; after 4:43 came the final ban in 5:90–91, to which Umar replied that they had stopped. | mentions 2:219, 5:90, 5:91
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p308#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | In the account related through Isra'il from Abu Ishaq and Amr ibn Shurahbil, Umar says the verse was revealed and the Prophet's caller announced that no drunk person should approach prayer; Abu Dawud transmits this wording.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · سعد بن أبي وقاص | reports | Sa'd reports that after an Anṣari hosted and served wine to migrants and Anṣar, they became drunk and boastful; a man struck Sa'd's nose with a camel jaw, and the verse then descended before wine was prohibited. Muslim transmits the full report; other Sunan collections transmit it except Ibn Majah.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | Ali reports that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf served food and wine; when the drunken group prayed, their reciter confused the words of al-Kafirun, prompting the verse. Al-Tirmidhi calls this version hasan sahih.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | Another account from Ali says he, Abd al-Rahman, and a third man drank before wine was forbidden; Abd al-Rahman led and garbled al-Kafirun, and the verse descended. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmit al-Thawri's route.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p309/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | A further report says Ali and companions drank at Abd al-Rahman's house before the ban; Ali led and failed to recite al-Kafirun properly, so the verse was revealed.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The best definition of intoxication is being unable to know what one is saying; drunkenness muddles recitation and removes reflection and humility.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أنس | reports | Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that a person who becomes drowsy in prayer should stop and sleep until able to know what he is saying; Bukhari and al-Nasa'i transmit it, and another wording warns he might curse himself while seeking forgiveness.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas interprets the exception as allowing a junub person to pass through a mosque without sitting; Ibn Kathir lists many authorities who agree, including Ibn Masud, Anas, Abu Ubayda, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Qatada, and others.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · يزيد بن أبي حبيب | reports | Yazid ibn Abi Habib says the verse addressed Anṣar whose homes opened into the mosque: when junub and without water, they had to cross the mosque to reach water.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A sound Bukhari report says the Prophet ordered every opening into the mosque closed except Abu Bakr's; Ibn Kathir links this late command to Abu Bakr's future leadership and need for mosque access.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | rejects | Ibn Kathir rejects reports that the Prophet ordered mosque doors closed except Ali's as mistaken; the sound report names Abu Bakr.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310#2/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Many imams say a junub person may not remain in a mosque but may pass through; menstruating and postpartum women are analogous.

R-FULL, d. 774 · بعض الأئمة | reports | Some authorities prohibit menstruating and postpartum women from passing through a mosque because of possible contamination.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن جرير | prefers | Ibn Jarir prefers wine intoxication and says the command addresses someone capable of understanding responsibility, not one so drunk that he cannot understand speech, who is legally like an insane person.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The legal address applies to one who understands speech, since understanding is a condition of legal responsibility; several legal theorists state this principle.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p310/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The verse may indirectly prohibit intoxication altogether: a regular drinker cannot consistently perform the five daily prayers at their times; Ibn Kathir compares this to the exhortation to prepare to die Muslim in 3:102. | mentions 3:102
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عائشة | reports | Aisha reports that when she said she was menstruating after the Prophet asked her to pass him a prayer mat from the mosque, he said menstruation was not in her hand; Abu Hurayra reports a similar exchange. [IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report transmitted by Abu Dawud through Aflat ibn Khalifa and Jasra from Aisha says a menstruating or junub person is not permitted in the mosque; Ibn Majah has a parallel route through Umm Salama.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو مسلم الخطابي | reports | Al-Khattabi says several scholars weaken the prohibition report because Aflat ibn Khalifa is unknown.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو زرعة الرازي | reports | Abu Zur'a says the commonly cited route through Jasra from Umm Salama is incorrect; the sound attribution is Jasra from Aisha.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | rejects | Al-Tirmidhi transmits a report telling Ali that only the Prophet and Ali may be junub in the mosque; Ibn Kathir says it is weak and unestablished because Salim ibn Abi Hafsa is abandoned and Atiyya is weak.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p311/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علي | reports | A second interpretation attributed to Ali takes the exception to mean a traveler who becomes junub and lacks water may perform prayer until water is available; reports from Ibn Abbas in one version, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others say likewise.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p312/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو ذر | reports | Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying clean earth purifies a Muslim even without water for ten years; when water is found, one should use it on the skin, which is better.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p312/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن جرير | prefers | After presenting both views, Ibn Jarir prefers that the junub person may cross the mosque; reading the exception as a traveler without water would repeat the separate tayammum ruling in 5:6. | mentions 5:6
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p312/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن جرير | holds | Ibn Jarir explains an abir al-sabil as one who passes and crosses through; Arabic uses the same root for crossing a road or river and calls a camel able to cross journeys abir asfar.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p312/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | prefers | Ibn Kathir endorses Ibn Jarir's reading as the majority view and the verse's apparent meaning: it bars prayer in a deficient state and entering its place while junub, except for passage through.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو حنيفة ومالك والشافعي | reports | Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Shafi‘i hold that a junub person may not remain in a mosque until bathing, or performing tayammum if water is unavailable or unusable.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أحمد | reports | Ahmad permits a junub person to remain in the mosque after performing wudu.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عطاء بن يسار | reports | Ataa ibn Yasar saw Companions sitting in the mosque while junub after performing prayer wudu; Ibn Kathir calls this report sound on Muslim’s criteria.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Illness permits tayammum when using water risks losing or damaging a limb, or prolonging recovery.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · بعض العلماء | reports | Some scholars permit tayammum for illness generally, relying on the verse’s broad wording.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid reports that the verse was revealed about an ill Ansari unable to stand for wudu and without anyone to bring him water; he asked the Prophet for help. Ibn Kathir grades the report mursal.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p313/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Travel permits tayammum whether the journey is long or short.
